# Chip accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

| Result                | Count |
| :-------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports           | 16    |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports | 8     |
| ❌ Does Not Support   | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable     | 31    |
| 🚩 Flagged            | 9/24  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **1.1.1 Non-text Content.** <!-- 1.1.1:gap:start -->The delete icon tells sighted users that the chip can be deleted. No text gives this information to a screen-reader user.<!-- 1.1.1:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum).** <!-- 1.4.3:gap:start -->`info` and `warning` labels are less than `4.5:1` in the `filled` and `outlined` variants. A letter avatar is `3.30:1`. On a focused `outlined` chip, all colors except `secondary` are less than `4.5:1`. On a hovered clickable `outlined` chip, `primary` is also less than `4.5:1`. The faded label of a disabled delete-only chip is `2.14:1`.<!-- 1.4.3:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.10 Reflow.** <!-- 1.4.10:gap:start -->The label does not wrap. At 320 CSS px, a label that fits a wide layout ends with an ellipsis.<!-- 1.4.10:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.** <!-- 1.4.11:gap:start -->The default delete icon is `1.86:1` on a `filled` chip and `1.88:1` on an `outlined` chip. The focused background is `1.61:1` against the page.<!-- 1.4.11:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.12 Text Spacing.** <!-- 1.4.12:gap:start -->The label does not wrap. With the WCAG text-spacing values, a label that fits at default spacing can end with an ellipsis.<!-- 1.4.12:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **2.4.3 Focus Order.** <!-- 2.4.3:gap:start -->The component does not move focus after a deletion. In the ChipsArray demo, a keyboard deletion moves focus to the page body.<!-- 2.4.3:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum).** <!-- 2.5.8:gap:start -->The delete icon is 22 px on a `medium` chip. It is 16 px on a `small` chip. On a clickable and deletable chip, the chip itself is a target, so the spacing exception does not apply.<!-- 2.5.8:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.** <!-- 4.1.2:gap:start -->The component does not set `aria-disabled` on a disabled delete-only chip. The chip stays focusable, and <kbd>Backspace</kbd> still deletes it. A delete-only chip has the button role, but <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> do nothing.<!-- 4.1.2:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- A chip renders its avatar or icon, its label, and its delete icon in DOM order.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through a set of chips.
2. Compare the focus order with the visual order.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->the focus order matches the visual order.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- A chip has a visible label, so users identify it by its text.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find product copy that refers to a chip.
2. Make sure that it names the chip label, not only its color or position.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->no instruction refers to a chip by color or position alone.<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.4.5:start -->

<!-- 1.4.5:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.5:pass:start -->the label is real text.<!-- 1.4.5:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 2.4.11:start -->

- A chip is an ordinary focusable element and does not put itself behind other content.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In a page with a sticky header, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a chip near it.
2. Scroll so that the chip is under the header.
3. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>.
4. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to move focus back to the chip.

<!-- 2.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.11:pass:start -->a part of the focused chip stays visible.<!-- 2.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 3.2.4 Consistent Identification · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 3.2.4:start -->

**Manual testing steps**

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.1.1 Non-text Content · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Chip.test.js`

<!-- 1.1.1:start -->

- The default delete icon is an `SvgIcon` with `aria-hidden="true"`, and it is not focusable. A unit test confirms `aria-hidden`. A pointer user clicks it. A keyboard user presses <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd> on the focused chip.
- The icon tells sighted users that the chip can be deleted. No text gives this information to a screen-reader user.
- A custom `deleteIcon` keeps its own attributes. Use an `SvgIcon`, or set `aria-hidden` on it.
- An `icon` is hidden. An `avatar` is not hidden, so its letter or its image `alt` becomes part of the name. Set `alt=""` on an image avatar when the label already gives the name.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a deletable chip.
3. Listen to the announcement.
4. Write down how a screen-reader user learns that the chip can be deleted.

<!-- 1.1.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.1.1:pass:start -->the screen reader tells the user that the chip can be deleted. Expected result from the source: it does not. To fix it, add a description with `aria-describedby`.<!-- 1.1.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `list` ✅, `listitem` ✅

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- A static chip is a `<div>` with no role. A clickable or deletable chip has the button role. A chip with `component="a"` and `href` is a link. Unit tests confirm the roles.
- A set of chips is not marked as a list. If the chips form a list, the author wraps them in `<ul>` and `<li>`, as the ChipsArray demo does.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader, move to a static, a clickable, and a link chip.
2. Listen to the role of each.
3. Move to a set of chips and listen for a list.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->each chip announces the correct role, and a list of chips is announced as a list.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.1 Use of Color · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.4.1:start -->

- The label and the icon give the meaning of a chip. The `color` prop only tints it.
- A selected filter chip that differs only by color loses its meaning without color. This is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Set the view to grayscale. In Chrome DevTools, open the Rendering tab, then select Emulate vision deficiencies > Achromatopsia.
2. Make sure that you can identify each chip and its state.

<!-- 1.4.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.1:pass:start -->the meaning and the state of each chip stay clear without color.<!-- 1.4.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Chip.test.js` · axe-core `color-contrast` ❌

<!-- 1.4.3:start -->

- A `filled` chip renders `contrastText` on `main`. An `outlined` chip renders `main` on the page. In both variants, `info` (`3.86:1`) and `warning` (`3.11:1`) are less than `4.5:1`.
- Unit tests compare the results with the [palette contrast contract](../../test/contrastContract.ts). Only these colors fail. axe-core `color-contrast` fails on the color fixture.
- The `default` color is `text.primary` on `action.selected`, about `13.9:1`.
- On a focused `outlined` chip, the background is `main` at `focusOpacity` (`0.12`) on the page, and the label stays `main`. Only `secondary` stays at `4.5:1` or more: `primary` `3.93:1`, `secondary` `5.21:1`, `error` `4.15:1`, `info` `3.33:1`, `success` `4.37:1`, `warning` `2.73:1`. A unit test confirms this set.
- On a hovered clickable `outlined` chip, the background is `main` at `hoverOpacity` (`0.04`). `primary` (`4.37:1`), `info` (`3.67:1`), and `warning` (`2.98:1`) are less than `4.5:1`. `secondary` is `5.92:1`, `error` is `4.69:1`, and `success` is `4.87:1`.
- A letter avatar in a chip renders `grey[700]` on `grey[400]`, `3.30:1`. axe-core marks one-letter text as incomplete, so the `ChipA11yKnownGaps` fixture uses a two-letter avatar to record the failure.
- A disabled chip is exempt. But a disabled delete-only chip still deletes on <kbd>Backspace</kbd>, so it is not an inactive component, and its faded label (`2.14:1`, measured by axe-core) is a real failure.
- All values are for the light palette.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure the label against the chip background, for each color and variant in use.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an `outlined` deletable chip, and measure the label against the focused background.
3. Move the pointer over an `outlined` clickable chip, and measure the label against the hovered background.
4. Measure the letter of any letter avatar.
5. Measure the label of any disabled delete-only chip.

<!-- 1.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.3:pass:start -->each label is at least `4.5:1` at rest, on hover, and on focus. `info` and `warning` fail. On an `outlined` chip, all focused labels except `secondary` fail, and the hovered `primary` label fails. The letter avatar and the disabled delete-only label fail.<!-- 1.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.4 Resize Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.4:start -->

- Under 200% page zoom, the chip, its container, and the label scale together, so a label that fits at 100% still fits. Page zoom decides the 1.4.4 rating (WCAG technique G142). The automated page-zoom check comes with the layout suite change in #49550, so this report confirms it with a manual step until then.
- Under text-only resize, the label grows but a px-wide container does not. The label does not wrap, so it ends with an ellipsis. In the `ChipA11yLongLabel` fixture, a label fits its 240 px container at 100% (177 px). At a 200% text size, 219 px of the 331 px label is visible. A Playwright test confirms this.
- A Playwright test confirms that the ChipsArray demo, with short labels, survives a 200% text-only resize.
- To make long labels safe under text-only resize, let the label wrap with `height: 'auto'` on the chip, and `display: 'block'` and `whiteSpace: 'normal'` on the label, as the MultilineChips demo does.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Render a chip with a label that just fits its container.
2. Set the browser zoom to 200%.
3. Make sure that the full label stays visible.

<!-- 1.4.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.4:pass:start -->the full label stays visible at 200% page zoom.<!-- 1.4.4:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- A chip is `inline-flex` with `maxWidth: 100%`, and its label does not wrap. At 320 CSS px, a label that fits a wide layout ends with an ellipsis. In the `ChipA11yLongLabel` fixture, 283 px of a 353 px label is visible. A Playwright test confirms this gap.
- A Playwright test confirms that the ChipsArray demo, which wraps its chips, does not scroll at 320 px. In a Playwright run, the ClickableAndDeletableChips demo, a row that does not wrap, scrolled by 6 px. This is a layout concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Render a chip with a long label at full width.
2. Set the viewport width to 320 CSS px.
3. Make sure that the full label stays visible.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.10:pass:start -->the full label stays visible. A long label fails with the default styles.<!-- 1.4.10:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Chip.test.js`

<!-- 1.4.11:start -->

- The delete icon is the only visual sign of the delete control. It is less than `3:1` in 8 of the 14 color and variant combinations, in the light palette:
  - `default` `filled`: `text.primary` at `26%` on `action.selected`, `1.86:1`.
  - `default` `outlined`: `1.88:1` against white.
  - Palette `filled`: `contrastText` at `70%` on `main`, `2.22:1` (`warning`) to `3.83:1` (`secondary`).
  - Palette `outlined`: `main` at `70%`, `2.23:1` to `3.57:1`.
- A unit test confirms that the default delete icon is less than `3:1`.
- On keyboard focus, the chip background gets darker. The focused `default` fill is `1.61:1` against the page.
- The `outlined` border is `grey[400]` (`1.88:1` against white), or `main` at `70%` (`2.23:1` to `3.57:1`). The label identifies the chip, so the border does not need `3:1`.
- With `focusVisible: true` on the theme, keyboard focus draws the theme outline ring instead. A Playwright test confirms the ring.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure the delete icon against the chip background.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a clickable chip.
3. Measure the focused background against the page.
4. Measure the `outlined` border against the page.

<!-- 1.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.11:pass:start -->the delete icon and the focus indicator are at least `3:1`. The `outlined` border does not need `3:1`, because the label identifies the chip. It is `1.88:1` (default) and `2.23:1` to `3.57:1` (palette). The default delete icon and focus indicator fail.<!-- 1.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 2.1.1 Keyboard · A

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Chip.test.js`, `ButtonBase.test.js`

<!-- 2.1.1:start -->

#### 2.4.3 Focus Order · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `Chip.test.js`

<!-- 2.4.3:start -->

- A static chip is not a tab stop. A clickable or deletable chip is one tab stop in DOM order, and a disabled clickable chip leaves the tab order. Unit tests confirm this.
- When a chip is deleted, the author's `onDelete` handler removes it. The component does not move focus. In the ChipsArray demo, a keyboard deletion moves focus to the page body. The author must move focus, for example to the next chip.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In the ChipsArray demo, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a chip.
2. Press <kbd>Backspace</kbd> to delete it.
3. Write down which element has focus.

<!-- 2.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.3:pass:start -->focus moves to a nearby chip or control, not to the top of the page. The ChipsArray demo fails.<!-- 2.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.7 Focus Visible · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 2.4.7:start -->

- On keyboard focus, a clickable or deletable chip gets a darker background. A Playwright test confirms that keyboard focus changes how a clickable chip looks.
- The change can be hard to see. For a `filled` `error` chip, the background changes from `#d32f2f` to `#c62828`. See 1.4.11.

#### 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: axe-core `target-size` ✅

<!-- 2.5.8:start -->

- A `medium` chip is 32 px high, and a `small` chip is 24 px high. axe-core `target-size` confirms the chips on the demos.
- The delete icon is a separate pointer target. It is 22 by 22 px on a `medium` chip, and 16 by 16 px on a `small` chip. axe-core does not check the icon, because it is not focusable.
- On a clickable and deletable chip, the chip itself is a target. A 24 px circle on the icon touches it, so the spacing exception does not apply. The equivalent exception does not apply either, because <kbd>Backspace</kbd> is not a pointer target.
- On a delete-only chip, the chip does nothing on click, so the spacing exception can apply.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In browser DevTools, select the delete icon of a `size="small"` chip.
2. Read the width and height of its box.

<!-- 2.5.8:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.5.8:pass:start -->the delete icon is at least 24 by 24 CSS px. Or, a 24 px circle on its center touches no other target. The default icon is 16 by 16 px.<!-- 2.5.8:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Chip.test.js` · axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-command-name` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-deprecated-role` ✅, `aria-hidden-focus` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-required-attr` ✅, `aria-roles` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `link-name` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- A clickable chip has the button role, and its label is the name. A disabled clickable chip has `aria-disabled="true"`. Unit tests confirm this.
- The component does not set `aria-disabled` on a disabled delete-only chip. The chip stays focusable, and <kbd>Backspace</kbd> still calls `onDelete`. A unit test confirms this gap.
- `skipFocusWhenDisabled` removes a disabled chip from the tab order, which also blocks <kbd>Backspace</kbd>. The state is still not exposed.
- A delete-only chip has the button role, but <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> do nothing.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> past a static chip. Make sure that focus does not stop on it.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a clickable chip, a deletable chip, and a disabled deletable chip.
4. Listen to the name, role, and state of each.
5. On the disabled deletable chip, press <kbd>Backspace</kbd>.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->each chip announces its label and "button". The disabled chip announces "disabled" and cannot be deleted. The disabled delete-only chip fails.<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** No auto-starting moving, blinking, or auto-updating content.
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.2 On Input (A).** <!-- 3.2.2:start -->A chip has no setting that the user changes. Deletion is an explicit action.<!-- 3.2.2:end -->
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A).** <!-- 3.3.2:start -->A chip is not a form field.<!-- 3.3.2:end -->
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.
- **4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).** Emits no status messages; state changes are covered by 4.1.2.

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), 44 px.** Chips are 24 or 32 px high, and the delete icon is 16 or 22 px. `🚩`
- **2.4.13 Focus Appearance.** The focused background differs from the resting background by `1.13:1` to `1.92:1`, which does not meet it. `🚩`

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 10.0.0-alpha.0.

<!-- scope:start -->

- **Scope.** The Chip component in isolation, rendered through its documented API.
- **Automated.** axe-core in the Playwright test harness, on the Chip demos and fixtures in [`chips.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/chips/chips.a11y.json). Interaction and contrast tests are in `Chip.test.js` and `ButtonBase.test.js`.
- **Assistive-technology review.** Not done yet. The flagged criteria come from a review of the source. A review with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver must still confirm them.

<!-- scope:end -->
